- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Overestimates prices after sharp spikes in history (e.g., post-85+ values), often overshooting by 5–10%.
- Shows persistent downward bias in the latter half of the forecast (last 10–15 days), suggesting mean reversion is not captured.
- Lags in response to recent price drops — forecasts remain high longer than actuals.
- Tends to overreact to short-term volatility, especially in the middle of the forecast window.
- Underestimates downward trends in the final 5–10 days, failing to account for momentum or policy-driven corrections.
- Sensitive to recent high values — forecasts often drop too slowly after peaks, missing the “rebound” or “correction” phase.
- Inconsistent with historical mean — model drifts below historical average in the last 10 days, suggesting calibration drift.
